editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks 10.70, Definition 10.70.1, which constructs both the graded Rees algebra and the affine chart associated with a chosen element of the ideal; these are different algebraic objects.

definitions.text: Given an ideal I of a commutative ring R, the Rees algebra of I is the nonnegatively graded R-algebra ⊕_{n≥0}I^n, with I^0=R and multiplication induced by the products I^m I^n⊆I^{m+n}.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: Rees algebra or blowup algebra of an ideal

definitions.text: For a∈I, the affine blowup algebra R[I/a] is the degree-zero part of the homogeneous localization of the Rees algebra ⊕_{n≥0}I^n at the degree-one element represented by a; its elements are represented by x/a^n with x∈I^n.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: affine chart algebra of a blowup

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks 10.141, Definition 10.141.1, which introduces small extensions of local Artinian rings; the rest establishes a lifting criterion equivalent to smoothness at a prime over a Noetherian base.

definitions.text: A small extension of local Artinian rings is a surjective local ring homomorphism B′→B whose kernel I has length one as a B′-module; consequently I²=0 and the maximal ideal of B′ annihilates I.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: small extension of Artinian local rings

definitions.text: For a finite-type ring map R→S with R Noetherian and prime q of S, smoothness at q is equivalent to having lifts of compatible R-algebra maps S→B across all surjections B′→B of local R-algebras with square-zero kernel, provided the maximal ideal of B lies over q.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: formal lifting characterization of smoothness at a prime

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks Categories 4.8, Definition 4.8.2 and Lemma 4.8.1. It defines a representable natural transformation of presheaves by requiring representability of its fibre products with every representable presheaf over the target.

definitions.text: For presheaves F,G:C^op→Sets, a natural transformation a:F→G is representable when for every object U in C and element ξ∈G(U), the fibre-product presheaf h_U×_G F formed using ξ:h_U→G is representable.
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: relatively representable natural transformation of presheaves

definitions.text: For natural transformations F→G and H→G of set-valued presheaves on C, their fibre product is the presheaf sending X to the set-theoretic fibre product F(X)×_{G(X)}H(X), with restriction maps inherited componentwise.
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: fibre product of presheaves

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks Topology 5.18, Definition 5.18.1, defining Jacobson spaces using density of closed points in each closed subset, not by requiring every point itself to be closed.

definitions.text: A topological space X is Jacobson if for each closed subset Z⊆X, the set of points of Z that are closed in X is dense in Z, so Z is its closure.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: Jacobson space

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks 10.133, Definitions 10.133.1 and 10.133.4, distinguishing finite-order differential operators on modules from their representing modules of principal parts.

definitions.text: For a ring map R→S and S-modules M,N, an R-linear map D:M→N is a differential operator of order at most k if k=0 and D is S-linear, or if k>0 and for every s∈S the commutator m↦D(sm)−sD(m) has order at most k−1.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: differential operator of finite order

definitions.text: For R→S, an S-module M and integer k≥0, the module of principal parts P^k_{S/R}(M) is the S-module representing differential operators of order at most k from M: Hom_S(P^k_{S/R}(M),N) is naturally identified with Diff^k_{S/R}(M,N).
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: order-k principal parts

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks 10.155, Lemmas 10.155.1 and 10.155.7 and the strict henselization construction. The universal Henselian enlargement preserves the residue field; its strict analogue uses a chosen separable closure of that residue field.

definitions.text: For a local ring (R,m), its henselization R^h is a Henselian local R-algebra initial among local R-homomorphisms from R into Henselian local rings, with maximal ideal mR^h and residue field canonically R/m; it may be constructed as a filtered colimit of suitable étale R-algebras.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: henselization of a local ring

definitions.text: After choosing a separable closure κ^sep of κ=R/m, the strict henselization R^sh of a local ring (R,m) is a strictly Henselian local R-algebra whose residue field is κ^sep and which satisfies the analogous universal local lifting property compatible with the chosen residue-field embedding.
definitions.source_section: Section 10.155 strict henselization construction and Lemma 10.155.10
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: strict henselization of a local ring

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks 10.52, Definitions 10.52.1 and 10.52.9, which separately define module length and simple modules via chains of submodules.

definitions.text: The length of an R-module M is the supremum of integers n for which M has a strictly increasing chain of R-submodules 0=M_0⊊M_1⊊⋯⊊M_n=M, with infinity if the possible lengths are unbounded.
definitions.context_hint: Module theory: length of an R-module

definitions.text: An R-module M is simple when M is nonzero and its only submodules are zero and M itself.
definitions.context_hint: Module theory: simple module

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks 10.40, Definitions 10.40.1 and 10.40.3, identifying support of a module and annihilators of elements or entire modules as distinct constructions.

definitions.text: For an R-module M, its support Supp_R(M) is the subset {p∈Spec(R):M_p≠0} of the prime spectrum, where M_p denotes localization at p.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: support of a module

definitions.text: For m in an R-module M, its annihilator Ann_R(m) is the ideal {r∈R:r·m=0}.
definitions.context_hint: Module theory: annihilator ideal of an element

definitions.text: For an R-module M, its annihilator Ann_R(M) is the ideal consisting of r∈R for which r·m=0 for every m∈M.
definitions.context_hint: Module theory: annihilator ideal of a module

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks Topology 5.13, Definition 5.13.1. The requirement is a fundamental system of quasi-compact neighbourhoods around each point; no Hausdorff hypothesis is imposed by the definition.

definitions.text: A topological space X is locally quasi-compact if every point x has a neighbourhood basis consisting of quasi-compact neighbourhoods: for every neighbourhood U of x, there exists a quasi-compact neighbourhood K of x contained in U.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: locally quasi-compact space

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks 10.138, Definition 10.138.1 and Lemma 10.138.5. Formal smoothness means existence of lifts of R-algebra maps across square-zero thickenings; uniqueness is not required.

definitions.text: A commutative ring homomorphism R→S is formally smooth if every R-algebra map S→A/I lifts to an R-algebra map S→A whenever A is an R-algebra and I⊆A satisfies I²=0.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: formally smooth ring map

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks Topology 5.7, Definitions 5.7.1, 5.7.8 and 5.7.10, which distinguish connected subsets and components, total disconnectedness, and local connectedness.

definitions.text: A nonempty topological space X is connected if it cannot be expressed as a disjoint union of two nonempty open subsets; equivalently its only clopen subsets are ∅ and X.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: connected space

definitions.text: A connected component of a topological space X is a connected subset maximal under inclusion among connected subsets of X.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: connected component

definitions.text: A topological space is totally disconnected if each of its connected components is a singleton.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: totally disconnected space

definitions.text: A topological space X is locally connected if each point x possesses a fundamental system of connected neighbourhoods.
definitions.context_hint: Topology: locally connected space

editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks 9.15, Definitions 9.15.1 and 9.15.8. Normal extensions and automorphisms over a subfield have distinct object types and are not synonymous.

definitions.text: An algebraic field extension E/F is normal if the minimal polynomial over F of each element α∈E factors completely into linear factors over E.
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: normal algebraic extension

definitions.text: For a field extension E/F, Aut(E/F) is the group, under composition, of field automorphisms σ:E→E satisfying σ(a)=a for every a∈F.
definitions.context_hint: Field theory: automorphism group of an extension
